name: Compensating microscope eyepieces
summary: Abbe designed microscope eyepieces with a deliberate colour error that cancelled the objective's leftover colour fringing, giving sharper colour-true images toward the edge of view.
description: Eyepieces deliberately given a color-dependent magnification opposite to the remaining lateral color difference of the objective, so the combined microscope image has less color error away from the axis.
tier_reason: A bounded technical contribution, transmission episode or documented configuration useful within a specific history; no broad dependence claim is established.

impact.note: A clear optical improvement used by microscopists in several countries, copied by a few other makers.

why: The new apochromatic objectives still magnified different colours slightly differently, which an eyepiece with the opposite error could cancel.

market.note: Zeiss offered this configuration for sale at stated prices in its 1889 catalogue. This supports commercial applicability but does not establish the first offer or a completed sale.

evidence.locator: printed p. 13 / PDF p. 16, List of Compensating Eye-pieces
evidence.supports: Priced list of the specific eyepieces; visual inspection.

date.basis: Abbe explains the construction in his 1886 paper; Zeiss retrospectively dates the named eyepiece introduction with the objectives to August 1886.

events.statement: Eyepieces deliberately given a color-dependent magnification opposite to the remaining lateral color difference of the objective, so the combined microscope image has less color error away from the axis.
events.caveats: This specific compensation design is not a claim that eyepiece correction was wholly new. Compatibility depended on objective and eyepiece properties, not the name alone.

evidence.locator: pp. 25–26, paragraphs on color amplification and its correction by an eyepiece
evidence.supports: Compensation principle and coordinated objective design.

links.statement: Zeiss introduced special compensating eyepieces for use with its new objective series; Abbe explains their coordinated correction of color-dependent magnification.
links.scope: Zeiss apochromatic objective–eyepiece system introduced in 1886.
links.alternatives: Dallinger also tried the compensating eyepieces on his existing objectives.
links.caveats: The direction indicates the stated companion configuration; neither component is claimed to have been invented earlier than the other.
links.timing: Both components were introduced together in 1886; this edge records combination, not chronological succession.

links.statement: Should astronomical optics connect to Abbe's microscope optics, or are these separate traditions?
links.caveats: Evidence needed: Abbe or Zeiss sources naming earlier achromatic theory.
links.finding: Newton describes a reflecting telescope response to refractive colour error; Abbe describes coordinated microscope objective and compensating-eyepiece correction. The checked sources do not document a transmission or development from that specific reflecting telescope to Abbe’s eyepiece design.
